title: Deal ops checklist for capacity tradeoffs (wip)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, seller + deal-ops facing checklist to run negotiations where the customer asks for guaranteed capacity (reserved) vs a blended burst + hosted API model. Focused on framing tradeoffs, callable scripts, and the minimum internal approvals needed to close pilots or early-stage contracts.

Audience:
- Sales engineers and AE in negotiations with platform/platform-ops/infra buyers (SRE, platform, procurement).
- Deal ops owner who needs a quick reference for capacity-related concessions and internal routing.

Quick TL;DR (1 sentence):
We trade predictable egress & latency (reserved) for committed rev + lower unit price; if customer values flexibility start with a pilot using burst + capped reserved cushion and clear SLA fallbacks.

What to surface in first call (5 mins):
- Who: which team owns infra decisions? (platform / infra / procurement)
- Workload shape: steady qps or spiky? expected peak token/sec and concurrency
- SLOs: 95th/99th latency targets, p50 throughput needs, and acceptable error budget
- Data/regulatory constraints that require Private/Dedicated or VPC
- Timeline: pilot -> production dates (try to pin three calendar milestones)

Premium talking points (seller script snippets):
- If they ask about cost: "Reserved capacity reduces per-token unit price and reduces variability — it’s ideal when you can predict baseline throughput for sustained savings. For spikes we provide burst capacity and graceful fallback to compatible model variants so customer-facing latency stays bounded."
- If they ask about risk: "We include rollback and canary policies in the contract plus runbook handoff; our dedicated pools are isolated and instrumented for binary search across versions to minimize regressions."
- If they press procurement: "We can structure commit bands (e.g., base commit + 20% flexible buffer) and include a quarterly reconciliation mechanism so you only pay for what you stabilize."

Negotiation checklist (step-by-step):
1) Confirm baseline commit number (tokens/day or GPU-hours/month). If customer cannot pick a baseline, propose a 3-month rolling commit that auto-adjusts after month 1 metrics.
2) Propose a buffer policy: reserved baseline + burst pool (percent-based) + overage pricing cap.
3) Decide model fallbacks: allow routing to lower-cost quantized model variant for non-critical paths. Document which routes are eligible.
4) Define latency SLOs and SLA credits: link to template wording in Confluence.
5) Agree on on-call and handoff deliverables for pilot: runbook, run-rate dashboard access, and 24/7 escalation for go-live week.
6) Legal checkpoints: data residency, KMS obligations, audit logging terms.
7) Commercials: commit term, unit price tiers, true-up cadence, and termination/transfer clauses for Dedicated capacity.

Pricing levers to propose (short):
- Commit term length (monthly vs annual)
- Commit size bands with stepped unit discounts
- Burst headroom % and burst pricing cap
- Model variant tiering (full FP vs int8 quantized pricing)
- Observability add-ons retention and SLA premium

Fallback playbook (if infra ops balks):
- Offer a short proof-of-concept: 4-week pilot capped spend, access to telemetry, and an ops-runbook review.
- If latency critical: propose dedicated capacity for the critical route + hosted fallback for secondary routes.
- If compliance blocks public cloud: propose Redwood Private with an on-prem connector trial for 6 weeks.

Risk & impact matrix (quick grid for call notes):
- Risk: unpredictable spiky load -> Impact: potential overage costs / throttling -> Mitigation: reserve cushion + auto-burst policy + token caps per request
- Risk: regression after model change -> Impact: customer-facing quality drop -> Mitigation: canary routing + rollback + prompt-level monitoring
- Risk: procurement wants no term -> Impact: high unit price -> Mitigation: pilot with usage caps + option to convert to commit within 90 days

Internal approvals required (minimum):
- Pricing approval from commercial lead (email + one-line summary)
- Legal signoff on residency/KMS obligations if flagged by security (link doc id)
- Infra capacity check from SRE (can we allocate the reserved pool this quarter?)

Templates & artifacts to attach when moving to proposal stage:
- Sample SOW language (Confluence link: confluence:GTMSALES-ops/sow-examples)
- SLA credit language snippet (Confluence link: confluence:GTMSALES-ops/sla-templates)
- Pricing bands spreadsheet (internal sheet: GTM-Pricing-Bands-2025)

Open questions (for deal owner to answer):
- Which specific endpoints must be pinned to Dedicated vs can be routed to hosted?
- What is the expected token distribution across routes? (short, medium, long responses)
- Do we need additional security certifications for pilot data?

Next steps (recommended cadence):
- AE -> send 1-pager with baseline commit proposal within 48 hrs
- SE -> provide expected latency/throughput delta for quantized variant within 72 hrs
- Deal ops -> draft commercial term (commit + buffer + true-up) and route to pricing for approval

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the initial commit deliberately conservative. Early oversell creates friction.
- Use the pilot telemetry to propose conversion path (X% of pilot baseline -> yearly commit).
- If procurement pushes annual assurance, swap some discount into observability retention instead of deeper price cuts.

Slack threads / refs that matter:
- #pilot-ops-discuss (thread: pilot-convert-2025-10)
- #pricing-approvals (ping: Liam O'Connor)

Status of this doc: working crib for SEs + deal-ops. Needs: pricing band spreadsheet linked, legal SOW snippet added, SRE capacity confirmation for Q4.

End of doc.
